title: Decoupled Causal Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2609.23535v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Causal discovery from observational data is a fundamental yet challenging task in scientific research. While existing approaches are primarily based on conditional independence tests, structure scores, or restrictive functional assumptions, we propose Decoupled Causal Discovery (DCD), a novel decoupling-based perspective that does not rely on these methodologies. DCD directly identifies the Markov boundary (MB) by decoupling non-target variables via weighting functions, such that only variables within the MB preserve dependence with the target under the decoupled distribution. Building on this, DCD iteratively constructs the Completed Partially Directed Acyclic Graph (CPDAG) by exploiting structural asymmetries within the MBs. We establish the theoretical identifiability, soundness, and completeness of DCD. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that DCD achieves strong performance, particularly excelling in challenging noise regimes.

translated_abstract: 从观测数据中进行因果发现是科学研究中一项基础但具有挑战性的任务。现有方法主要基于条件独立性检验、结构评分或限制性函数假设，我们提出了解耦因果发现（DCD），这是一种新颖的基于解耦的视角，不依赖于这些方法论。DCD通过加权函数对非目标变量进行解耦，直接识别马尔可夫边界（MB），使得在解耦分布下只有MB内的变量与目标保持依赖关系。在此基础上，DCD通过利用MB内的结构不对称性，迭代构建完全部分有向无环图（CPDAG）。我们建立了DCD的理论可识别性、可靠性和完备性。实证评估表明，DCD取得了优异的性能，特别是在具有挑战性的噪声环境中表现突出。
tldr: 提出了一种不依赖条件独立性检验、结构评分或函数假设的解耦因果发现方法DCD，通过加权函数解耦非目标变量直接识别马尔可夫边界，并利用结构不对称性迭代构建CPDAG，在噪声环境下表现尤为出色。
en_tdlr: Proposes Decoupled Causal Discovery (DCD), a novel approach that directly identifies the Markov boundary by decoupling non-target variables via weighting functions and iteratively constructs the CPDAG using structural asymmetries, without relying on conditional independence tests, structure scores, or functional assumptions, achieving strong performance especially under challenging noise regimes.
